extraction.name: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation)
extraction.description: POPE is an object hallucination evaluation benchmark for large vision-language models that converts hallucination evaluation into a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes-or-No questions about objects in images. It includes three sampling strategies (random, popular, and adversarial settings) to probe whether models hallucinate objects.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by selecting 500 images from the MSCOCO validation set, generating polling-based yes/no questions about object presence using ground-truth annotations and three sampling strategies (random, popular, adversarial) for negative objects. SEEM was also used to automatically annotate images from MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA for extended evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images and ground-truth object annotations from the MSCOCO validation set, as well as images from A-OKVQA and GQA datasets. Segmentation results were also generated using the SEEM automatic segmentation tool.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth objects are extracted either from human annotations or with automatic segmentation tools. Negative sampling is conducted for nonexistent objects under Random/Popular/Adversarial settings. Ground-truth and nonexistent objects are formulated into question templates to poll LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluation uses F1 Score and accuracy metrics; performance of LVLMs consistently decreases from random to popular to adversarial settings, consistent with findings about hallucination of frequently appearing and co-occurring objects.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 6 questions per image (3 ground-truth objects and 3 nonexistent objects)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (automatic segmentation tool) used for automatic annotation of ground-truth objects
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The object distributions of visual instructions affect object hallucination in LVLMs. Evaluation results might be affected by the corresponding data distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation focuses only on object hallucination and cannot measure overall LVLM performance. Models are evaluated on a subset of validation data. The matching-based method may fail when LVLMs don't explicitly answer 'Yes' or 'No'. Automatic segmentation tool annotations may be inconsistent with human annotations. Only a small number of LVLMs are compared.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination in LVLMs hinders their safe use in real-world deployment and can harm user experiences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset (POPE) is intended for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), specifically for testing whether models generate objects inconsistent with ground-truth images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Negative (nonexistent) objects are sampled using three strategies: random sampling, popular sampling (frequently occurring objects), and adversarial sampling (objects likely to be hallucinated).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Ground-truth objects are extracted from human annotations and segmentation masks; polling-based yes/no questions are constructed from these objects for evaluation.

name.evidence: we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination

description.evidence: The basic idea is to convert the evaluation of hallucination into a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes-or-No short questions about the probing objects (e.g., Is there a car in the image?). We show that such a method is more stable and flexible.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Given an input image, POPE first extracts ground-truth objects in the image either from human annotations or with the help of automatic segmentation tools like SEEM. Then, POPE conducts negative sampling for nonexistent objects in the image under Random/Popular/Adversarial settings. Finally, the ground-truth objects and nonexistent objects are formulated into question templates to poll LVLMs.
